title: Photonic weight storage for optical neural networks
bottleneck: Optical neural networks compute with light, but their weights must be stored and updated somewhere: volatile tuning burns constant power, while nonvolatile phase-change materials suffer from limited endurance, drift, and slow write speeds. There is no photonic equivalent of SRAM that holds weights indefinitely with fast, unlimited updates at low energy.
why_it_blocks: Without efficient weight storage, photonic accelerators either burn power holding weights or stall on slow reprogramming, erasing their speed and efficiency advantage over electronics. Large-model photonic inference is blocked until weight memory is solved.
current_state: Phase-change materials (GST and successors) integrated on waveguides demonstrate nonvolatile photonic memory in labs, and research into electro-optic and MEMS-based storage continues. Endurance and drift at scale are unresolved.
